# Data Source: stripe_billing_meter_event_summary

The aggregated usage a billing meter recorded for one customer over a time window. Look one up by the `meter`, the `customer` and the window's `start_time` and `end_time`, which Stripe requires to fall on minute boundaries. Stripe aggregates events about a minute after they are sent, and a window with no events may have no summary, which is an error.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "stripe_billing_meter_event_summary" "october" {
  meter      = "mtr_123"
  customer   = "cus_123"
  start_time = 1790812800 # 2026-10-01T00:00:00Z
  end_time   = 1793491200 # 2026-11-01T00:00:00Z
}

output "api_calls_in_october" {
  value = data.stripe_billing_meter_event_summary.october.aggregated_value
}
```

## Argument Reference

This data source supports the following arguments:

* `customer` - (Required) The ID of the customer whose usage the summary aggregates.
* `end_time` - (Required) End timestamp for this event summary (exclusive). Must be aligned with minute boundaries.
* `meter` - (Required) The ID of the parent object.
* `start_time` - (Required) Start timestamp for this event summary (inclusive). Must be aligned with minute boundaries.

## Attribute Reference

This data source exports the following attributes in addition to the arguments above:

* `aggregated_value` - Aggregated value of all the events within `start_time` (inclusive) and `end_time` (inclusive). The aggregation strategy is defined on meter via `default_aggregation`.
* `id` - Unique identifier for the object.
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.
